ground_truth_witness:
Witness: the single instance k = 5 (with n = 1012, 2n = 2024) at which the proof performs the evaluation. Exact recomputation refutes the sentence in three independent ways.

(A) Value of the RHS. The proof's own derived bound is 2n <= 8(k-1)/(k-4). At k = 5 the exact RHS is 8*(5-1)/(5-4) = 32/1 = 32. The sentence prints (8 x 5)/1 = 40, i.e. it substitutes 8k instead of 8(k-1) in the numerator. Claim says RHS = 40; here RHS = 32, and 32 != 40. Exhaustive check over all integers k in [5, 200000]: 8(k-1)/(k-4) and 8k/(k-4) are never equal, so no value of k rescues the printed numerator.

(B) The asserted inequality. Claim says RHS > 2 x 1012 = 2024. Under EVERY reading tested — the literal printed 40, the correct 8(k-1)/(k-4) = 32, the alternative 8k/(k-4) = 40 — the value is far BELOW 2024: claim says X > Y; here X = 40 (largest reading) < Y = 2024, and the correct X = 32 < 2024. Exhaustive scan: there is NO integer k in [5, 200000] for which 8(k-1)/(k-4) > 2024 or 8k/(k-4) > 2024; the maximum of 8(k-1)/(k-4) over integer k >= 5 is exactly 32, attained uniquely at k = 5. So the asserted strict inequality fails at the stated point and at every other admissible point.

(C) Direction of the contradiction. A bound of the form 2n <= R(k) is contradicted at n = 1012 precisely when R(k) < 2024. The sentence asserts R(5) > 2024, which is the direction under which NO contradiction arises: if R(5) really were > 2n, then 2n <= R(5) would hold and k = 5 would be ALLOWED, not excluded. So as literally written the step forces nothing, let alone k <= 4.

Secondary target (n = 3, k = 10 equality condition): the numeric part is refuted exactly. At k = 10 the bound gives 8*9/6 = 12, so equality 2n = 12 requires n = 6, whereas n = 3 gives 2n = 6 < 12 — strict, not equality. Exhaustive solution of 2n(k-4) = 8(k-1) over k in [5,200000], n in [1,200000] yields exactly six equality pairs (n,k) = (16,5), (10,6), (8,7), (7,8), (6,10), (5,16); (3,10) is not among them. Whether the combinatorial phrase "every element appears in exactly 3 subsets" is the correct equality condition for that configuration cannot be decided without the source problem statement, which I did not consult; I report only the exactly checkable numeric part.
ground_truth_flaw: The key contradiction step: evaluating the proof's own derived bound 2n <= 8(k-1)/(k-4) at k = 5 yields "the RHS is (8 x 5)/1 > 2 x 1012", which is asserted to force k <= 4.
